- Overestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral, especially after recent spikes; reduce forecast by 5–15% in such contexts.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative or after a sharp drop; adjust upward by 5–10% if recent sentiment turns bearish.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings; if sentiment shifts sharply, delay or dampen forecast adjustments for 2–3 periods.
- When sentiment is positive and prices are rising, reduce forecast peak by 10–20% to avoid overshoot; sentiment-driven spikes often overcorrect.
- Mean-reversion bias is common in 30-day forecasts; if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, reduce forecast by 5–10% across all horizons; sentiment-driven declines are often not fully reflected in model.
- Forecast should not exceed 15% above or below the 18-day moving average unless sentiment strongly supports deviation.
